html:
1What You Will Learn

Note

Acronyms in this note. API: application programming interface; LLM: large language model; MCP: Model Context Protocol; SDK: software development kit

  • What the exam is: 53 items, 120 minutes, a scaled score of 720 to pass
  • The eight domains, their weights and the 26 skills behind them
  • The minimally qualified candidate the exam is written for
  • The developer decision rules that explain most correct answers
  • How the course is built and how to use it

Who this exam is for. A hands-on developer, usually with one to five years of software engineering and at least six months with Claude, who builds, integrates and ships Claude applications: API integration, agents and tools, prompts and context, evals, security and model selection. It is not for casual users of Claude or for roles limited to prompt writing.

2The Exam at a Glance

Fact Value (guide v1.0, July 2026)
Credential / code Claude Developer – Foundations / CCDV-F
Items 53, multiple choice and multiple response; each item says how many answers to select
Time 120 minutes (about 2 minutes 15 seconds per item)
Passing score 720 on a scaled range of 100 to 1,000 (criterion-referenced: a fixed standard, not a ranking)
Fee USD 125 per attempt [Verify live]
Delivery Proctored by Pearson VUE: online or at a test center
Validity 12 months from the date the credential is awarded
Retakes Wait 14 days after the first failed attempt, 30 after the second, 90 after the third; at most 4 attempts in a rolling 12 months; limits are per exam
Prerequisites None are required; experience is recommended, and the credential is awarded on exam performance alone
Score report Pass or fail, the scaled score, and the percent correct per domain (domain figures do not decide pass or fail)

Who can sit it [Verify live]. Exams are open to people at organizations in the Claude Partner Network who register with a company email. Others can take the free Anthropic Academy courses, which give completion certificates, not the credential. This course teaches the same knowledge to everyone.

Exam tip

For a multiple-response item the stem says how many answers to select: read that number first, then choose exactly that many.

3The Eight Domains

Domain Weight Skills (weight) Modules

D5 Model Selection and Optimization 16.8% LLM Fundamentals 5.2 · Technical Fundamentals 6.1 · Model Selection and Tradeoffs 2.7 · Cost and Token Management 2.8 7, 8
D1 Agents and Workflows 14.7% Agent Architecture 4.5 · Agent Construction with Claude 5.3 · Agent Patterns and Frameworks 4.9 5, 6
D6 Prompt and Context Engineering 11.0% Context Engineering 3.8 · Prompt Engineering 4.6 · Output Handling 2.6 9, 10
D8 Tools and MCPs 10.6% Tool Implementation 4.4 · MCP Server Development 2.1 · Agentic Customization 4.1 11, 12
D7 Security and Safety 8.1% AI Application Security 3.2 · Guardrails and Safe Deployment 2.3 · Claude Hooks 1.0 · Identity, Secrets and Key Management 1.6 13, 14
D3 Claude Code 3.1% Claude Code Operation 3.1 15
D4 Eval, Testing and Debugging 2.6% Debugging and Error Handling 2.6 16
  • Of 53 items, about 17 to 18 come from D2, 9 from D5, 8 from D1, 6 from D6, 6 from D8, 4 from D7, and 1 to 2 each from D3 and D4.
  • Weights are the approximate share of scored items. Each skill has a short description in the guide; items are written against it.
  • Study order by value: D2 (a third of the exam), then D5, D1, D6, D8 and D7; D3 and D4 together are under 6%.
Exam tip

Spend study time in proportion to the weights: the Applications and Integration domain alone is worth about as much as Agents and Prompt and Context together.

4The Minimally Qualified Candidate

Running case

Tidewater Insurance

  • Throughout the course you follow Tidewater Insurance, a fictional insurer
  • Its developers build a claims assistant: it reads claim documents, looks up policies through tools, answers adjusters and must keep customer data safe
  • Each module solves one problem of this application; the questions use the same style as the exam

The minimally qualified candidate (MQC) can:

  • build agents and workflows with the Claude Agent SDK and agentic frameworks
  • integrate Claude through the API and client SDKs, including streaming and error handling
  • operate Claude Code and author Skills, CLAUDE.md, settings.json and plugins
  • write effective prompts, apply context engineering, and validate output
  • design and run evals and debug failure modes
  • choose models, manage tokens, caching and batches
  • apply secure-by-design controls, including hooks, against prompt injection and destructive actions
  • build custom tools and MCP servers, and weigh built-in tools, custom tools, Skills and MCP

5Ten Decision Rules the Questions Reward

Most items describe a requirement or a failure and ask for the best approach. The best answer usually follows one of these rules. Each later module shows them at work.

# Rule Typical wrong answers
1 Match the API to the latency need: synchronous for waiting users, batch for non-urgent bulk work Parallel synchronous calls to save time or money
2 Match the model to the task: the smallest model that meets the quality bar, with evals to prove it; step up when evals fail "Always the largest model", "always the smallest"
3 Cache stable prefixes; keep volatile text after them Putting timestamps before the cached text
4 Treat retrieved content as untrusted data, keep it apart from trusted instructions, and limit what injected text can do (least privilege, hooks) Asking the user not to attack, changing temperature, bigger model
5 Enforce hard rules in code (hooks, validation, permissions), not in prose Stronger prompt wording
6 Validate output: structured outputs and schemas, defensive parsing, skepticism toward confident text Trusting the first answer
7 Find where the failure lives (integration layer or model output) with traces before changing prompts Rewriting the prompt for an HTTP error
8 Keep context small and relevant: prune tool output, compact, isolate in subagents Sending the whole history forever
9 Reuse through the right mechanism: MCP for shared external capabilities, Skills for procedures, custom tools for app-specific functions Hard-coding logic in prompts
10 Secrets stay out of code and prompts: secrets manager, environment variables, least-privilege keys, rotation Keys in source or client-side code
Exam tip

When two options both work, prefer the one that is enforced, measured, least-privileged and cost-aware.

6How to Use This Course

  • Order: read modules 1 to 16 in order (they follow the domains), then module 17 (recap) and 18 (technique).
  • Each module has the skills it covers, a case, tables, figures, Exam tips, scenario questions with explanations and a Quick Reference Card.
  • Build something. The guide recommends building and operating at least one Claude application that uses the API, one or more tools, basic prompt and context engineering, and simple security and evaluation practice.
  • Product details change fast. Boxes marked [Verify live] show current behavior (for example model IDs, thinking modes, cache rules). On the exam, answer as the guide teaches and check the official documentation for current details.
  • Independence. This course is independent study material; it is not affiliated with, endorsed by or sponsored by Anthropic or Pearson VUE. Read the official exam guide, the Certification Terms and Conditions and the Exam Policy before you register.

7Exam Q&A

S1A candidate has three years of software engineering experience and no earlier Anthropic credential. Does the exam guide set a prerequisite they fail?

  • AYes: a prior Claude credential is required
  • BYes: five years of experience are required
  • CNo: there are no mandatory prerequisites for the exam
  • DYes: a mandatory Anthropic course must be completed first
Show the answer

Answer: C. The guide recommends experience but requires no prerequisites; eligibility to register is a separate matter (partner organization).

S2Which domain carries the largest share of the scored items?

  • AModel Selection and Optimization
  • BTools and MCPs
  • CApplications and Integration
  • DAgents and Workflows
Show the answer

Answer: C. Applications and Integration is 33.1%, about a third of the exam.

S3A candidate scored 700 on the exam but 90 percent in one domain. What is the result?

  • APass, because one domain is high
  • BFail, because the total scaled score is below 720
  • CFail, because each domain must also reach 720 on its own
  • DPass, because domains average out
Show the answer

Answer: B. The pass decision uses the total scaled score; domain percentages are only reported for guidance.

S4Which statement best describes the minimally qualified candidate?

  • AA casual user who writes prompts in the chat application and shares them with colleagues
  • BA data scientist who trains custom models
  • CA hands-on developer who builds, integrates and ships Claude applications
  • DA manager who approves AI projects
Show the answer

Answer: C. The exam targets builders; it excludes casual users and roles limited to prompt writing.
